method: Bounded Family-level landscape, not a systematic review per Driver. Sources below were inspected through the stated access depth; exact claims require separate deep-research rows.

INF-F01.constructs: Availability, actual encounter, duration, salience and selective exposure are different variables.
INF-F01.mechanisms: Opportunity to encounter depends on distribution and choice; attention and processing are downstream contingencies.
INF-F01.measurement: Separate offer, click/encounter, dwell and recall logs.
INF-F01.boundaries: Choice and prior attitude moderate exposure; available information is not actual exposure.

INF-F02.constructs: Arrival rate, message length, density and window-relative volume are message/environment properties, not occupied cognitive capacity.
INF-F02.mechanisms: Task demands and irrelevant content can increase processing competition.
operations: vary amount while holding task and content stable
INF-F02.measurement: Count content and window separately from workload measures.
INF-F02.boundaries: The evidence includes multi-component display changes and clinical settings; no universal overload threshold.

INF-F03.constructs: Clarity, surface language, conceptual complexity, audience-relative readability and uncertainty disclosure.
INF-F03.mechanisms: Decoding and comprehension depend on message features and audience capability; uncertainty format changes perceived uncertainty.
INF-F03.measurement: Pilot uses feature-specific text and claim-bound uncertainty contrasts.
INF-F03.boundaries: Reuse INF-F03 governed pilot; INF-013/INF-077 overlap and blocked metadata remain unresolved.

INF-F04.constructs: Attribute, gain/loss, sequence, metaphor and numeric/visual framing are distinct manipulations.
INF-F04.mechanisms: Reference points, pragmatic inference and task representation can change judgments.
operations: hold propositions fixed while varying representation
INF-F04.measurement: Check equivalence of compared descriptions and task outcome.
INF-F04.boundaries: Risky-choice results do not imply stable risk preference or universal direction; formats and complements can reverse effects.

INF-F05.constructs: Evidence quality, amount, relevance, logical strength, counterargument and refutation are separable.
INF-F05.mechanisms: Argument evaluation depends on relevance, processing ability and competing arguments.
operations: vary one evidence or argument component while holding conclusion fixed
INF-F05.measurement: Objective quality coding must not be replaced by recipient acceptance.
INF-F05.boundaries: Most messages bundle components; strong and weak arguments can interact rather than add.

INF-F06.constructs: Disclosure, provenance, source identity, credentials, reliability and perceived credibility are distinct.
INF-F06.mechanisms: Cues can change credibility only when noticed and interpreted; actual traceability needs verifiable chain.
operations: vary source label or quantified uncertainty disclosure
INF-F06.measurement: Measure receipt of cue separately from perceived source credibility.
INF-F06.boundaries: Field label effects can be limited; verbal and numeric uncertainty differ.

INF-F07.constructs: Repetition count, spacing, delay, cross-source consistency and source independence are distinct.
INF-F07.mechanisms: Repeated encounter can increase familiarity and context-dependent truth/confidence judgments.
operations: repeat the same proposition with declared spacing and source
INF-F07.measurement: Separate presentation count from verified encounter and from belief confidence.
INF-F07.boundaries: Psychological repetition contribution already exists and is blocked from additive activation; no duplicate candidate.

INF-F08.constructs: Narrative form, coherence, causal structure, exemplification, vividness and emotion are not interchangeable.
INF-F08.mechanisms: Engagement and counterarguing may mediate message response.
operations: compare narrative packages with controlled nonnarrative material
INF-F08.measurement: Code message components and recipient transportation separately.
INF-F08.boundaries: Most comparisons bundle multiple narrative features; no component-specific efficacy inferred.

INF-F09.constructs: Cultural match, language accessibility, local specificity and personalization differ from perceived relevance.
INF-F09.mechanisms: Tailoring can improve fit to individual needs, but packages combine assessment, feedback and content.
operations: match declared recipient attributes to message content
INF-F09.measurement: Measure actual match, perceived relevance and outcome separately.
INF-F09.boundaries: Small heterogeneous package effects do not identify a single component; RDS language accessibility needs calculation rule.

INF-F10.constructs: Threat severity, susceptibility and response-efficacy claims are content, not the corresponding appraisals.
INF-F10.mechanisms: Fear-appeal packages can change risk appraisals and downstream responses under moderators.
INF-F10.measurement: Keep each claim component and perceived counterpart separate.
INF-F10.boundaries: Meta-analytic package efficacy does not isolate individual content components or transfer to all hazards.

INF-F11.constructs: Descriptive prevalence claims, consensus, comparative benchmarks and performance feedback are different from actual Social norms.
INF-F11.mechanisms: A credible referent-group prevalence statement can update perceived descriptive prevalence toward the stated value.
operations: present a specified referent-group prevalence statistic
INF-F11.measurement: Specify group, behavior, baseline estimate, message receipt and follow-up estimate.
INF-F11.boundaries: Actual group prevalence, subjective norm and behavior must not be conflated; feedback packages may bundle own-behavior comparison.

INF-F12.constructs: Objective veracity, selective omission, correction presence, specificity and explanation are distinct from belief accuracy.
INF-F12.mechanisms: Corrections can reduce misinformation influence but leave residual influence; format and timing matter.
INF-F12.measurement: Use same proposition and time point; retain null and contrary findings.
INF-F12.boundaries: No universal debiasing or generic backfire inference; active Psychological explanatory-refutation effect is reused.

INF-F13.constructs: Instruction specificity, steps, timing and call-to-action are content features, not actual plans or behavior.
INF-F13.mechanisms: An enacted implementation plan can improve behavior, but instruction exposure alone is a different treatment.
operations: supply specified steps or timing cues
INF-F13.measurement: Distinguish message receipt, plan formation and completed action.
INF-F13.boundaries: Implementation-intention program evidence cannot be attributed to a single guidance component.
